add_comment_reaction.description: Add an emoji reaction to a comment on a Figma file, such as a thumbs up or a check mark, to show it has been seen or dealt with without posting a reply.
add_comment_reaction.display_str_template: React {2} to comment {1} in Figma file {0}.
add_comment_reaction.name: add_comment_reaction

parameters.description: The Figma file the comment is on. A file key or a full Figma file URL both work.
parameters.name: file_key

parameters.description: The comment's ID, from 'List comments', 'Post comment' or the New comment trigger.
parameters.name: comment_id

parameters.description: The emoji, written as its shortcode: :+1: for a thumbs up, :heart:, :white_check_mark: and so on. A skin tone can follow, as in :+1::skin-tone-2:.
parameters.name: emoji

emoji.description: The reaction, as its shortcode (for example :+1:).

status.description: Always 'success' when Figma took the change.

delete_file_comment.description: Delete a comment from a Figma file by its comment id. Only the comment's author (or a file admin) can delete it. Deleting a top-level comment also removes its replies. Useful for cleaning up automated or resolved comments.
delete_file_comment.name: delete_file_comment

parameters.description: The Figma file the comment is on. A file key or a full Figma file URL both work.
parameters.name: file_key

parameters.description: The id of the comment to delete (from 'List Figma comments' or the response of 'Post Figma comment').
parameters.name: comment_id

export_images.description: Turn frames or layers of a Figma file into PNG, JPG, SVG or PDF images, and get a download link for each. The links last 30 days. Useful for sending the latest design to a channel, a document or a review.
export_images.name: export_images

parameters.description: The Figma file the frames are in. A file key or a full Figma file URL both work.
parameters.name: file_key

parameters.description: Which frames or layers to export, by their node ids, separated by commas (e.g. '1:2,1:8'). In Figma, select a frame and copy its link: the id is the node-id in the link, with the dash written as a colon.
parameters.name: node_ids

parameters.description: The kind of image to make. Defaults to PNG.
parameters.name: image_format

parameters.description: How large to make the image, from 0.01 to 4 times its size in Figma. Defaults to 1. Ignored for SVG.
parameters.name: scale

images.description: One image per frame or layer, in order.

url.description: A link to download the image, for 30 days. Empty when Figma couldn't render that layer.

get_file.description: Get a Figma file's metadata and document tree by its file key. Returns the file name, the editor type (design, whiteboard, or slides), the last-modified timestamp, the current version id, a thumbnail URL, and the node tree (pages and their layers). Large files can return a lot of data, so use 'depth' to fetch only the top levels of the tree. Useful for reading a file's structure, checking when it last changed, or grabbing its thumbnail.
get_file.name: get_file

parameters.description: The Figma file to read. Paste either the file key (the slug in a file URL) or a full Figma file URL such as https://www.figma.com/design/AbC123/My-File; the key is extracted automatically.
parameters.name: file_key

parameters.description: How many levels of the document tree to return. 1 returns just the pages, 2 also returns each page's top-level layers, and so on. Leave blank to return the entire tree (which can be very large).
parameters.name: depth

parameters.description: A specific version id to fetch (from the file's version history). Leave blank for the current version.
parameters.name: version

parameters.description: Set to 'paths' to include vector geometry for each node. Leave blank to omit geometry (smaller response).
parameters.name: geometry

parameters.description: Comma-separated node ids (e.g. '1:2,1:8') to return only those nodes, their children, and their ancestor chains instead of the whole document (much smaller when you care about a few frames). Top-level pages are always included. Leave blank to return the full tree (subject to 'depth').
parameters.name: ids

returns.description: File metadata plus the document node tree. The 'document' node is the root; its children are the file's pages (CANVAS nodes).

branches.description: Present only when requested with branch_data: metadata for the file's branches. Each item is {key, name, thumbnail_url, last_modified, link_access} (note: snake_case, unlike the camelCase top-level fields).

componentSets.description: Map of node id -> component-set metadata.

components.description: Map of node id -> component metadata, telling you which component each instance comes from.

document.description: Root DOCUMENT node. Its 'children' are the pages (CANVAS nodes).

editorType.description: Which editor the file uses: 'figma', 'figjam', or 'slides'.

lastModified.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last edit.

mainFileKey.description: Present only when the file is a branch (requires branch_data): the key of the main file.

role.description: The caller's role on the file: 'owner', 'editor', or 'viewer'.

styles.description: Map of style id -> style metadata used in the file.

thumbnailUrl.description: URL of a rendered thumbnail image of the file.

version.description: The current version id of the file.

get_file_comments.description: List the comments on a Figma file, including each comment's text, author, creation time, whether it has been resolved, and where it is pinned on the canvas. Replies are returned as their own comments with a 'parent_id' pointing at the thread's first comment. Useful for triaging design feedback or pulling open comments into a review.

comments.message: Can we bump the hero headline to 48px?

get_file_comments.name: get_file_comments

parameters.description: The Figma file whose comments to list. A file key or a full Figma file URL both work.
parameters.name: file_key

parameters.description: Turn on to return each comment's text as its markdown equivalent where applicable. Leave off for plain text.
parameters.name: as_md

returns.description: The file's comments, newest activity first.

client_meta.description: Where the comment is pinned. One of: a canvas point (Vector) {x, y}; a frame offset {node_id, node_offset: {x, y}}; a Region {x, y, region_height, region_width}; or a FrameOffsetRegion. Null for a reply.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the comment was created.

file_key.description: Key of the file the comment belongs to.

order_id.description: Ordering key Figma uses to sort comments.

parent_id.description: Id of the parent comment when this is a reply; empty string for a top-level comment.

resolved_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the comment was resolved, or null if unresolved.

email.description: Email address; present on /me, may be absent on comment authors.

get_me.description: Get the Figma user that the connected access token belongs to, including their id, display handle, email, and avatar URL. Useful for confirming which account a workflow is acting as, or as a lightweight connection check.
get_me.name: get_me

email.description: Email address; present on /me, may be absent on comment authors.

post_file_comment.description: Post a comment on a Figma file, or reply to an existing comment. Provide the file and the message text; optionally reply within an existing thread by giving that comment's id. Returns the created comment, including its new id. Useful for leaving automated design feedback or notifying reviewers from a workflow.
post_file_comment.display_str_template: Post a comment to Figma file {0}.
post_file_comment.name: post_file_comment

parameters.description: The Figma file to comment on. A file key or a full Figma file URL both work.
parameters.name: file_key

parameters.description: The comment text to post.
parameters.name: message

parameters.description: To reply inside an existing thread, enter the id of the comment you are replying to. This must be a root comment (you cannot reply to a comment that is itself a reply). Leave blank to start a new top-level comment.
parameters.name: comment_id

client_meta.description: Where the comment is pinned. One of: a canvas point (Vector) {x, y}; a frame offset {node_id, node_offset: {x, y}}; a Region {x, y, region_height, region_width}; or a FrameOffsetRegion. Null for a reply.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the comment was created.

file_key.description: Key of the file the comment belongs to.

order_id.description: Ordering key Figma uses to sort comments.

parent_id.description: Id of the parent comment when this is a reply; empty string for a top-level comment.

resolved_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the comment was resolved, or null if unresolved.

email.description: Email address; present on /me, may be absent on comment authors.

remove_comment_reaction.description: Take back a reaction you added to a comment on a Figma file. Figma removes only your own reaction, never someone else's.
remove_comment_reaction.display_str_template: Remove the {2} reaction from comment {1} in Figma file {0}.
remove_comment_reaction.name: remove_comment_reaction

parameters.name: file_key

parameters.description: The comment's ID, from 'List comments', 'Post comment' or the New comment trigger.
parameters.name: comment_id

parameters.description: The emoji, written as its shortcode: :+1: for a thumbs up, :heart:, :white_check_mark: and so on. A skin tone can follow, as in :+1::skin-tone-2:.
parameters.name: emoji

remove_comment_reaction.result_str_template: Removed the reaction from the Figma comment.

emoji.description: The reaction, as its shortcode (for example :+1:).

description: Collaborative interface design. Read a Figma file's structure and metadata, export frames as images, list and post comments for design review, clean up comments, and start workflows on new comments, all with a personal access token.

figma_new_comment_trigger.description: Runs for each new comment on a Figma file, replies included unless you leave them out, with its text, who wrote it and where it's pinned. Comments already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.author: Who wrote it (their Figma name).
output.author_email: Their email address, when Figma shares it.
output.file_url: A link to the file in Figma.
output.is_reply: Whether it's a reply in a thread.
output.node_id: The frame or layer it's pinned to, if any.
output.parent_id: The comment it replies to; empty for a new thread.

parameters.description: The Figma file to watch: paste its link, or the file key from the link.
parameters.name: file_key

parameters.description: Whether a reply in a thread starts the workflow too, or only a new top-level comment.
parameters.name: replies
